points: **Topical corticosteroids** on the face are the commonest trigger; also inhaled or nasal steroids, and heavy moisturisers or foundations.
Fluorinated toothpaste and barrier disruption may contribute.
Monomorphic 1–2 mm red papules, papulovesicles and pustules on a red, sometimes scaly background.
Around the mouth, nasolabial folds, chin; may involve the sides of the nose and eyelids (**periocular**).
**Vermilion sparing**: a narrow clear rim around the lips.
Burning or tightness more than itch; no comedones.

cards.name: Rosacea
cards.clue: Older; flushing; central face; no clear perioral rim

cards.name: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
cards.clue: Greasy scale in nasolabial folds and brows

cards.name: Contact dermatitis
cards.clue: Itch, eczematous, linked to a product

items.t: Granulomatous or periocular disease not responding, or diagnostic doubt: dermatology.

pearls.t: Pharmacists often spot inhaled-steroid perioral dermatitis: advise rinsing and wiping the face after inhalers.
Hydrocortisone makes it look better briefly, then worse.
